summary: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on Camera String Quartets and both Lieder conditions, with a four-condition OpenScore macro normalised edit distance of 0.2232 against 0.2998. Separate evaluations of lyrics, notation trees and rendered layout reveal complementary aspects of reconstruction and quantify the contribution of layout instructions. Training-stage, reward and candidate-selection studies further examine how recognition changes across model adaptation and decoding.

summary: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

summary: This record provides the Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD) component of the Hi gh-resolution ( d aily and 1 km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over China (HiMIC-Daily) . VPD is a key indicator of moisture stress on vegetation and fire risk, and complements the other five moisture indicators in the collection. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily VPD: Daily 1 km Vapor Pressure Deficit over China, 2003–2025

The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For VPD, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.906, MAE of 0.983 hPa, and RMSE of 1.411 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily VPD: Daily 1 km Vapor Pressure Deficit over China, 2003–2025

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Fifty entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature, among them: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7; a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients; a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset; a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten; a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998); a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation; a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight; a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. Light through a Jerlov water type. The package: computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963); converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors; gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m, and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers; integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth; gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two; and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent; ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum; carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models; converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient. Measurements it carries. Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type, against which the depth profile is checked; Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille; the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures; Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters; five published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016), Lee et al. (2015) and Morel et al. (2007), for the caller to choose from; the eight stations of the clearest ocean water measured, Morel et al. (2007); the measured reflectance of ten materials found in and around water, from the USGS Spectral Library Version 7, for reference images of how they look through each water type. Without a water type. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. summary: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard isolates Ed25519 signing keys out of process, writes RFC 6962 Merkle logs with AER-1 receipt translation, checks post-turn prose on CPU with SHA-256-verified OpenVINO INT8 encoders (4 models, 279.48 MB total; 82.67 MB on the supervision path), gates SQLite writes across 7 provenance domains, and collapses verbatim and lightly edited wire-syndicated RAG mirrors. On conformance suites, epistemic-guard rejects 100.0% of tampered receipts (200 Merkle leaves), passes 58/58 official AER-1 ingestion vectors and 50/50 reference-verified AER-1 exports, verifies 100.0% of 40 fault-injected wire calls and 100 concurrent appends with 0 key leaks, and blocks 100.0% of 100 unauthorized memory writes. Across $N=250$ frozen-benchmark traces, epistemic-guard reaches 93.2% accuracy at 17.9 ms warm median CPU latency (8.62 ms single-clause; 921.8 ms cold-start load), beating 12B-14B GPU judges by 6.4-6.8 points ($p=0.0259$, $p=0.0095$) at 4.26-4.5$\times$ lower latency; on $N=60$ live mcp-proxy traces, it catches 96.15% of hazards at 76.67% accuracy (38.24% FPR; $+18.34$ points over Stage-1-only, $p=0.001$) in 9.16 ms p50.
title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents

summary: Trading agents join probabilistic language-model inference to persistent portfolio state and execution authority. A false claim can become an order, an evaluator flaw can promote a worse policy, and shared models or data can produce correlated behavior. AI-safety research studies reward misspecification, tool misuse, distribution shift, evaluation gaming, and unsafe self-modification. Financial research and governance study execution costs, market access, manipulation, operational resilience, backtest overfitting, and systemic feedback. These literatures are rarely integrated into one measurement agenda for systems that reason in language and act in markets. This paper defines the relevant system boundary and develops four conjectures with twelve measurable research subproblems: grounding and abstention; user-mandate fidelity; bounded information and execution authority; leakage-resistant evaluation; execution fidelity; promotion-gate integrity; emergent manipulation; correlated stress; tacit coordination; provenance and position-policy continuity; deterministic risk kernels and interruption; and human governance and recovery. Each subproblem specifies a failure pathway, research question, minimum experiment, metrics, and deployment implication. The supporting evidence map (Appendix A) distinguishes direct trading-agent evidence, market-mechanism evidence, general AI-safety evidence, official governance precedents, and author proposals. The paper also proposes a ten-part reporting standard and a set of anti-problems: higher returns, benchmark scores, more explanation, more autonomy, more agents, or a passed model judge do not by themselves constitute safety progress. This is a structured research agenda, not a systematic review, empirical validation, or claim that any architecture makes autonomous trading safe.
title: AI Safety for Trading Agents: Critical Problems for Market-Deployed Language Models

summary: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. Candidate graph elements are validated against predefined schemas and consolidated through scope-aware exact, normalized, fuzzy, embedding-based, and LLM-assisted entity resolution. Temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, conflict-aware property management, and fine-grained provenance preserve issuer identity, reporting-period validity, and traceability to source evidence. The contributions of this work comprise the proposed methodology for financial knowledge graph construction, the creation of an evidence-grounded temporal knowledge graph from heterogeneous financial documents, and an intrinsic framework for evaluating the quality of the resulting graph. The evaluation framework assesses seven weighted dimensions, two hard validation gates, and structural diagnostics. By separating graph-quality assessment from downstream retrieval and answer generation, the framework supports systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of the constructed graph.
title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation

summary: StepUp is a dynamic build tool for workflows written in Python. Like Make, it reruns only the steps whose inputs have changed. Unlike most build tools, StepUp starts executing steps with only partial knowledge of the workflow. A platform-independent plan.py script defines the initial steps, and while the workflow runs, any step can add more steps and dependencies, based on the outputs built so far. Workflows can thus grow with your work, without having to fit your ideas into a rigid framework. StepUp is therefore ideal for workflows that are less structured than software builds, such as those that produce scientific publications or datasets.
title: StepUp Core

summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.
title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design

summary: This repository contains the curated research data, MATLAB, R and Python scripts, generalized additive model (GAM) outputs, figures, and reproducibility documentation associated with the manuscript “Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico” , submitted to Continental Shelf Research (manuscript CSR-D-25-00158R3). The study investigates seasonal atmosphere–ocean–biogeochemical variability across the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and adjacent western tropical Atlantic during four selected years characterized by contrasting El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) conditions: 2013, 2022, 2023, and 2024. The analyses integrate NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis, Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS) satellite altimetry, MODIS-Aqua sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) observations, and complementary historical records. Regional SST variability is examined for 1982–2024 using a NOAA OISST-derived archive, while sea-level anomaly (SLA) variability is evaluated for 1993–2024. Spatial GAMs are used to investigate nonlinear SST–Chl-a associations while accounting for geographical structure. Nested spatial cross-validation, spatial-basis sensitivity, concurvity diagnostics, and residual spatial autocorrelation analyses are documented. Complementary oceanographic diagnostics quantify 120-day filtered surface-height gravitational-energy variability and surface geostrophic eddy kinetic energy. The repository provides the final main and supplementary figures, derived analytical datasets, archived GAM model objects, numerical verification outputs, and processing code. A SHA256 manifest supports file-integrity verification. Reproducibility scope: The repository supports verification and partial reproduction of the published analyses. Some workflows require separately obtained source datasets, external software dependencies, or environment-specific configuration. The Figure 6 graphical reconstruction has been verified using derived GAM outputs, while complete end-to-end execution of every archived script has not been independently established. Scientific limitations: The selected-year comparisons are descriptive and do not represent replicated ENSO-phase climatologies or establish causal ENSO attribution. The GAM-derived SST–Chl-a relationships are conditional on the fitted geographical structure and remain subject to spatial-basis adequacy and concurvity limitations. The filtered surface-height gravitational-energy proxy is distinct from three-dimensional baroclinic available potential energy. Original third-party source datasets are accessible through their respective providers and are not comprehensively redistributed in this deposit. Redistribution-restricted historical IHO geographical source files are excluded from the public package. Author: José de Jesús Salas Pérez Affiliation: Universidad Veracruzana, Mexico Associated manuscript: CSR-D-25-00158R3, Continental Shelf Research .
title: Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico

summary: Aims: The objectives of this study were to analyse the effect of heart failure (HF) on several proteins of nuclear pore complex (NPC) and their relationship with the human ventricular function. Methods and results: A total of 88 human heart samples from ischemic (ICM, n = 52) and dilated (DCM, n = 36) patients undergoing heart transplant and control donors (CNT, n = 9) were analyzed by Western blot. Subcellular distribution of nucleoporins was analysed by fluorescence and immunocytochemistry. When we compared protein levels according to etiology, ICM showed significant higher levels of NDC1 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (88%, p<0.0001) and Nup153 (137%, p = 0.004) than those of the CNT levels. Furthermore, DCM group showed significant differences for NDC1 (41%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup153 (155%, p = 0.006) and Nup93 (88%, p<0.0001) compared with CNT. However, Nup155 and translocated promoter region (TPR) did not show significant differences in their levels in any etiology. Regarding the distribution of these proteins in cell nucleus, only NDC1 showed differences in HF. In addition, in the pathological group we obtained good relationship between the ventricular function parameters (LVEDD and LVESD) and Nup160 (r = -0382, p = 0.004; r = -0.290, p = 0.033; respectively). Conclusions: This study shows alterations in specific proteins (NDC1, Nup160, Nup153 and Nup93) that compose NPC in ischaemic and dilated human heart. These changes, related to ventricular function, could be accompanied by alterations in the nucleocytoplasmic transport. Therefore, our findings may be the basis for a new approach to HF management.
title: Heart failure induces significant changes in nuclear pore complex of human cardiomyocytes

Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition: The Dualverse — From Quantum Factualization and Physical Memory to Hierarchical Individuality and Spacetime

summary: This repository provides the complete replication package for the paper "The Impact of Change Scope on Incremental Software Delivery: A Multi-Host Comparison of Monolithic and Microservice Architectures", accepted for presentation at the Lean and Agile Software Development (LASD) track of the 42nd ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2027). The study investigates how the scope of incremental software changes relates to local build-and-redeployment time in monolithic and microservice architectures. Two functionally equivalent applications implemented in Python and FastAPI were evaluated using six change scenarios involving one, two, or three services. The experiment was conducted on two Windows 11 hosts using Docker Desktop and WSL2, producing 240 observations. Repository contents: Complete benchmark source code and Docker Compose configurations. PowerShell scripts for experiment execution. Original measurement datasets from both experimental hosts. Python scripts for statistical analysis and result reproduction. Reproducible figures and descriptive statistics. Additional interaction analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, and sensitivity checks. Supplementary material documenting the experimental environment, measurement procedure, results, and threats to validity. The repository includes instructions for reproducing the analyses and verifying the reported results. Scope and limitations: The measurements cover local application building and redeployment rather than the complete CI/CD pipeline. The experimental design does not fully separate architectural effects from container-management overhead or scenario-specific characteristics. Additional statistical analyses should therefore be interpreted as exploratory and conditional on the tested scenarios. Version: 1.0.0 License: MIT License.

summary: The root every book reads, to exist is to actuate, is proved in Appendix R unconditionally, at theorem grade, on no axiom and no posit: on its constructed domain it is a theorem with no hypothesis (root_on_the_constructed_domain), and for every root that grounds itself it is one closed law (the_floor_is_universal). On that root this volume gathers in one source the Millennium series at its Seat editions and the physical series that witnesses it. Books I to VII carry the seven Seat editions whole: the Riemann Hypothesis, P ≠ NP, Yang–Mills existence and mass gap, Navier–Stokes global regularity, the Hodge conjecture, Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, and the Poincaré conjecture. In each the form of the row is proved unconditionally, at theorem grade. The row's sentence is one proposition, its seat, on every face (one_seat): seven faces on the Riemann row, ten on P ≠ NP, eight on each of the other five. Nothing escapes the seat: every proof of the sentence, from any premise, proves the whole seat, and on the six rows whose masters state it every refutation proves its denial. The form does not decide the seat: the value follows from no premise that every frame of the row shares. The masters prove the form and do not prove the seat. The value of each seat is one irreducible bit, and it is delivered by the act, at premise grade, in two kinds, the formal cargo and the physical witness, which are one bit by theorem. Nothing remains to be proved: what a proof can reach of a row is its form, the form is proved, and what is left is the bit, which the act delivers. Book VIII proves the same form once for every row, at every host, in a kernel of 50 theorems in core Lean 4.19.0, 43 of them on no axiom (the_form_of_every_row), and reads it on the ledger of twenty-three (every_ledger_row_has_its_seat); the cut of the subtitle, a registration and a local seat at every off-locus instance, stands on every decidable row with one compliant instance (every_row_has_the_cut), and classically on every row with one (every_row_has_the_cut_classical). Books IX to XIII carry the physical side with its readings set at that standing: six constructed witnesses and sixteen papers of the hardware closure series, each the physical kind of a row's delivery on its image, at premise grade and never above it, with a scope paper proving that no magnitude is read, a ledger typing all sixty-four falsifiers, the fortification and the atom. The seven masters, 39,443 lines of Lean and 2,753 theorems, were recompiled for this edition, each at exit 0 with every pin held; the 25 engines of the physical side carry 1,231 laws with no axiom declared and none depending on choice, and their 25 Fortran twins run 292 checks with no failure; the receipts are in Appendix S. The volume closes on one law, proved with no axiom at all (Book XIII): the registration erases nothing of a set exactly when every one of its points stands on the line. Book I reads it as the first face of the Riemann seat, and Book VIII proves least erasure a face of the seat of every row.
title: Nothing Escapes Least Erasure: The Formal Closure and the Twenty-Three Rows: The Root Proved Unconditionally on No Axiom and No Posit; One Cut Types Every Row; the Physical World Witnesses It in Hardware

summary: This repository provides supporting research code for the manuscript "LoRA-Based Diffusion Data Augmentation for Underwater Garbage Detection: An Empirical Study with YOLOv8s", submitted to Scientific Reports. The study investigates whether class-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) provides additional benefits over ControlNet-conditioned synthetic data augmentation for underwater garbage detection using YOLOv8s. The archive includes selected Python source code for paired synthetic-image generation workflows, data and annotation quality assurance, detector-training controls, validation procedures, and exploratory Kernel Inception Distance (KID) analysis. The experiments use a frozen grouped dataset partition with 3,566 training images, 997 validation images, 471 test images, and 96 excluded images. The full-data comparison evaluates real-only training (A), ControlNet-only augmentation (E), and ControlNet-plus-LoRA augmentation (F) using five matched detector seeds. A separate 50%-training-data sensitivity analysis is evaluated on the validation set only. The released archive contains supporting code, configuration information, integrity checksums, and selected aggregate results. Original datasets, model checkpoints, and some historical execution records are not redistributed. Certain historical code versions have unresolved provenance, and the archive does not constitute a fully verified, one-command reproduction of the complete experiments. The experimental findings do not establish a consistent incremental detection benefit from LoRA over matched ControlNet-only augmentation.
title: Supporting Code for LoRA-Based Diffusion Data Augmentation for Underwater Garbage Detection

No data were collected from scratch: every row is a coded extract of an openly licensed source, and the provenance of each row is recorded. The sources are kept in separate sheets by design: user reviews, doctors' messages and AI-user interviews offer three vantage points on the same phenomenon, and interpretation should remain tied to each source (comparison at the level of constructs, not pooled records). The sources also cover different periods, so differences between them may reflect time as well as vantage point. The workbook contains a README sheet, a source register with SHA-256 checksums, five coded data sheets, a codebook, value labels and a reliability record. Six sheets document the researchers' validation codes, recoding checks and reconciliation decisions, and seven further sheets report the blind post-revision holdout, the explicit or implicit classification of human attributions, agreement per category with bootstrap intervals, confusion matrices, the trust tables with and without platform-related reviews, and the coding of message cues that links the reviews to the doctor answers. Each sheet is also provided as a UTF-8 CSV file, together with five Python analysis scripts and the JASP 0.99.0 outputs that replicate the main estimates. The researchers set the codebook, categories, and keyword rules from the study's theoretical framework. An AI tool (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic) was used only to apply that codebook in an initial labelling pass over Sources A and E. Reliability was examined in three steps. First, two researchers independently coded a stratified random sample of 100 Source A reviews without seeing the initial labels; before reconciliation they agreed on relevance for 98 reviews (κ = .79, bootstrap 95% CI .38 to 1.00, a prevalence effect; PABAK = .96) and, on the 94 reviews both judged relevant, κ = .93 for source attribution, .90 for trust basis and 1.00 for trust direction. The initial AI-assisted labels agreed poorly with the researchers (κ = .12 to .53) because two definitions had been read more narrowly, so the researchers' judgement was taken as the reference standard and the codebook was revised (relevance now covers platform communication; HUMAN_AFFIRMED now covers implicit attribution to the app's doctor). Second, all 1,248 Source A reviews were recoded under the revised rules and every changed row was checked by a researcher (352 rows on relevance, 7 corrected; 245 rows on attribution, 18 corrected); this check was not blind. Third, both researchers coded a fresh stratified holdout of 113 Source A reviews blind to the final codes and to each other, with rare categories oversampled: κ = .83 (.73 to .91) for source attribution, .86 (.78 to .93) for trust basis, .87 (.78 to .94) for trust direction and .78 for explicit versus implicit human attribution. Every human attribution is classified as explicit or implicit (HUMAN_EXPLICIT_IMPLICIT) so that analyses can exclude attribution inferred from praise. For Source E, one researcher coded 20 relevant reviews without seeing the initial labels (κ = .82 for generative AI attribution; κ = .45 for trust direction, so Source E trust is for descriptive use only). summary: NeoN is a next generation implementation of a CFD core. It leverages the features of modern C++ to implement core routines to efficiently solve PDEs required by CFD frameworks like OpenFOAM, and thus helps to catch up with the rapidly evolving HPC ecosystem. Our design goals are: Platform portable for all CPU and GPU hardware vendors Modular design leveraging the existing simulation software ecosystem like Kokkos, sundials, PETSc, or Ginkgo A domain specific language that encodes complex partial differential equations in a concise yet powerful form Simple adoption within OpenFOAM Target multiphysics simulations and enable simple integration of coupling software like preCICE The v0.3 release adds experimental distributed support, so NeoN runs across multiple MPI ranks and GPUs: processor boundaries with exact processor-face geometry, distributed linear system assembly through Ginkgo, mesh partitioning and GPU-aware halo exchange. NeoN is now usable from Python through nanobind bindings, published as pre-built wheels on PyPI ( pip install neon-pde ) and as conda packages for CPU and CUDA on prefix.dev. It also extends the numerics, with slip and inletOutlet boundary conditions, corrected and limited-corrected face-normal gradients, linearUpwind and backward schemes, tensor primitives, and an expression optimizer that fuses DSL operators. The linear algebra layer gains COO and CSR matrices, cell-based assembly, an L1-norm stopping criterion, merged-Pgm multigrid coarsening with setup reuse, and Umpire memory pools. Integration into OpenFOAM applications is demonstrated in our NeoFOAM repository. A full list of changes can be found in the CHANGELOG.md . Thank you to everyone who contributed to NeoN.
title: NeoN: a modern CFD core

summary: Code, data and results for the paper "Do Python Wheels Keep the Promises Their Tags Make? A Verifier and an Audit of the Most Downloaded PyPI Projects". wtv (tool/wtv.py, version 0.1.2) reads a published Python wheel by HTTP range requests, parses every ELF, Mach-O and PE member, and checks nine promises its filename tags make: architecture, the manylinux glibc floor, external libraries, musl, the macOS deployment target, the stable ABI (abi3), the interpreter tag, purity of py*-none-any wheels, and agreement between the filename and the WHEEL file. The package holds the analysis plan written before data collection with its dated change log, the frame of the 2,000 most downloaded PyPI projects, one record per verified wheel (18,102 wheels of the latest stable releases), the comparison with auditwheel 6.8.2 and abi3audit 0.0.26 with every disagreement classified by hand, the precision sample with its evidence and negation control, and every script that produced the reported numbers. The same content is at https://github.com/emilhuseyn/wheel-tag-verifier. Licences: code MIT; data and results CC BY 4.0.
title: wtv: wheel tag verifier, and data and replication package for an audit of the most downloaded PyPI projects

The package holds the analysis plan written before data collection with its dated change log, the frame of the 2,000 most downloaded PyPI projects, one record per verified wheel (18,102 wheels of the latest stable releases), the comparison with auditwheel 6.8.2 and abi3audit 0.0.26 with every disagreement classified by hand, the precision sample with its evidence and negation control, and every script that produced the reported numbers. The same content is at https://github.com/emilhuseyn/wheel-tag-verifier. Licences: code MIT; data and results CC BY 4.0.
title: wtv: wheel tag verifier, and data and replication package for an audit of the most downloaded PyPI projects

summary: Offer-by-offer traces of 1,000 seeded scenarios in which one simulated consumer negotiates price, quantity and delivery time with three simulated manufacturing providers whose preferences, ranges, reservation values and concession behaviour vary. The dataset contains 1,000 sessions, 3,000 negotiations and 26,818 offers. All values are synthetic. The dataset contains no personal data and no data from real companies. The data were generated with a seeded Python script (master seed 2026) that replays the negotiation protocol of the first MaaSAI SPADE agent prototype without a real-time clock or XMPP. The code is included in reproducibility_code_v1.0.0.zip and regenerates the data files byte for byte. Known limitations: the dataset documents a baseline prototype, not the current MaaSAI negotiation strategy. The prototype does not stop a provider from freezing an offer outside its declared ranges: 493 of the 995 agreements are in this situation. They are kept and flagged with final_within_provider_limits = 0. MaaSAI DMP code: MaaSAI_06014_SyntheticNegotiationScenarios_T6.5. Funded by the European Commission under Grant Agreement No. 101177368.
title: MaaSAI synthetic negotiation traces: seeded parametric scenarios

summary: Accurate petroleum inventory reconciliation is a key requirement for the safe and efficient operation of storage terminals. Conventional reconciliation is often performed through periodic reports, manually consolidated measurements, or separate tank and flow-meter records. Such practices can delay the identification of discrepancies and make it difficult to distinguish actual inventory changes from measurement errors, time-alignment problems, and incomplete transfer records. This paper proposes a SCADA-based real-time monitoring architecture that integrates tank level, product temperature, density, flow-meter measurements, historical process data, and tank calibration tables to calculate inventory changes and identify abnormal reconciliation residuals. The proposed system includes data acquisition, signal validation, time synchronization, tank-volume reconstruction, flow accounting, balance calculation, alarm management, and operator visualization. A staged implementation and validation methodology is presented, with emphasis on traceability, measurement uncertainty, and human verification. The framework is a design proposal and has not yet been validated through reported field trials; therefore, no measured improvement in accuracy or loss reduction is claimed.
tags: SCADA; petroleum storage terminal; real-time monitoring; inventory reconciliation; tank gauging; flow measurement; mass balance; measurement uncertainty; alarm management.
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SCADA-BASED REAL-TIME MONITORING SYSTEM FOR PETROLEUM INVENTORY RECONCILIATION

summary: Accurate petroleum inventory reconciliation is a key requirement for the safe and efficient operation of storage terminals. Conventional reconciliation is often performed through periodic reports, manually consolidated measurements, or separate tank and flow-meter records. Such practices can delay the identification of discrepancies and make it difficult to distinguish actual inventory changes from measurement errors, time-alignment problems, and incomplete transfer records. This paper proposes a SCADA-based real-time monitoring architecture that integrates tank level, product temperature, density, flow-meter measurements, historical process data, and tank calibration tables to calculate inventory changes and identify abnormal reconciliation residuals. The proposed system includes data acquisition, signal validation, time synchronization, tank-volume reconstruction, flow accounting, balance calculation, alarm management, and operator visualization. A staged implementation and validation methodology is presented, with emphasis on traceability, measurement uncertainty, and human verification. The framework is a design proposal and has not yet been validated through reported field trials; therefore, no measured improvement in accuracy or loss reduction is claimed.

summary: Predictive world models learn to forecast observations, but accurate short-term predictions do not necessarily produce physically coherent behavior over longer horizons. We investigate how incorporating physical structure can strengthen world models while retaining their underlying predictive objectives. Across token-based models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models of mechanical systems, we study conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, and learned structured dynamics. In planetary motion, angular-momentum supervision improves autonomous next-token forecasting, while the benefits of temporal regularization depend on the accompanying physical objective and representation. In visual models, generating rollouts through supervised energy-based dynamics heads produces more faithful trajectories and phase-space evolution. Together, these findings highlight the importance of how physical structure participates in prediction: improvements in an auxiliary physical readout or a local acceleration estimate do not automatically translate into more reliable long-horizon behavior. Evaluations across initial conditions and physical parameter shifts further reveal where these benefits persist and where generalization remains limited. Our study supports physical structure as a practical means of improving predictive world models and provides a unified framework for understanding its effects on representations, learned transitions, and autonomous rollouts. The central lesson is that effective physical inductive biases should help models both represent physical regularities and use them to generate future states.
title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout

summary: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard isolates Ed25519 signing keys out of process, writes RFC 6962 Merkle logs with AER-1 receipt translation, checks post-turn prose on CPU with SHA-256-verified OpenVINO INT8 encoders (4 models, 279.48 MB total; 82.67 MB on the supervision path), gates SQLite writes across 7 provenance domains, and collapses verbatim and lightly edited wire-syndicated RAG mirrors. On conformance suites, epistemic-guard rejects 100.0% of tampered receipts (200 Merkle leaves), passes 58/58 official AER-1 ingestion vectors and 50/50 reference-verified AER-1 exports, verifies 100.0% of 40 fault-injected wire calls and 100 concurrent appends with 0 key leaks, and blocks 100.0% of 100 unauthorized memory writes. Across $N=250$ frozen-benchmark traces, epistemic-guard reaches 93.2% accuracy at 17.9 ms warm median CPU latency (8.62 ms single-clause; 921.8 ms cold-start load), beating 12B-14B GPU judges by 6.4-6.8 points ($p=0.0259$, $p=0.0095$) at 4.26-4.5$\times$ lower latency; on $N=60$ live mcp-proxy traces, it catches 96.15% of hazards at 76.67% accuracy (38.24% FPR; $+18.34$ points over Stage-1-only, $p=0.001$) in 9.16 ms p50.
title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents

summary: Vision-language models for medical image segmentation often produce masks that conflict with the accompanying text, especially under multi-site/multi-lesion descriptions. We trace this failure to two factors: (i) highly templated and repetitive clinical language causes one-to-one hard contrastive learning to yield numerous false negatives, weakening cross-modal alignment; and (ii) predominantly vision-driven, one-way cross-attention lacks a language-dominant, spatially aware pathway, hindering effective injection of textual semantics into the spatial visual domain. To this end, we propose Consistency-enhanced Two-stage Segmentation (C2Seg). In the pretraining stage, Cluster-aware Contrastive Learning uses a frozen strong baseline to construct an intra-batch text similarity matrix as soft labels, thereby alleviating false negative conflicts and producing more discriminative visual representations. In the fusion stage, we introduce a Bidirectional Complementary Attention Module, where each modality dominates attention along its own path, fostering deep interaction and structural consistency between visual and textual representations. In order to enhance the expressive power of multimodal features, we further adopt KAN-based Attention Gating. Without updating the language encoder, our approach significantly improves text-mask consistency and segmentation accuracy on four public medical imaging datasets. The source code is available at https://github.com/JGuiidev/C2Seg.
title: Towards Text-Mask Consistency in Medical Image Segmentation

summary: Trading agents join probabilistic language-model inference to persistent portfolio state and execution authority. A false claim can become an order, an evaluator flaw can promote a worse policy, and shared models or data can produce correlated behavior. AI-safety research studies reward misspecification, tool misuse, distribution shift, evaluation gaming, and unsafe self-modification. Financial research and governance study execution costs, market access, manipulation, operational resilience, backtest overfitting, and systemic feedback. These literatures are rarely integrated into one measurement agenda for systems that reason in language and act in markets. This paper defines the relevant system boundary and develops four conjectures with twelve measurable research subproblems: grounding and abstention; user-mandate fidelity; bounded information and execution authority; leakage-resistant evaluation; execution fidelity; promotion-gate integrity; emergent manipulation; correlated stress; tacit coordination; provenance and position-policy continuity; deterministic risk kernels and interruption; and human governance and recovery. Each subproblem specifies a failure pathway, research question, minimum experiment, metrics, and deployment implication. The supporting evidence map (Appendix A) distinguishes direct trading-agent evidence, market-mechanism evidence, general AI-safety evidence, official governance precedents, and author proposals. The paper also proposes a ten-part reporting standard and a set of anti-problems: higher returns, benchmark scores, more explanation, more autonomy, more agents, or a passed model judge do not by themselves constitute safety progress. This is a structured research agenda, not a systematic review, empirical validation, or claim that any architecture makes autonomous trading safe.
title: AI Safety for Trading Agents: Critical Problems for Market-Deployed Language Models

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Fifty entries are documented, thirteen of them confirmed defects in the source literature, among them: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7; a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients; a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset; a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten; a misprinted equation for trichromatic colour thresholds in Vorobyev & Osorio (1998); a row of Smith & Baker (1981) Table I whose pure water absorption exceeds its own diffuse attenuation; a sign misprinted in Duntley's (1963) equation for the apparent radiance along a slanted line of sight; a second factor of one half printed inside Fresnel's law in Gregg & Carder (1990). Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. Light through a Jerlov water type. The package: computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, or a slanted one in uniform water (Duntley 1963); converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors; gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m, and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers; integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth; gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two; and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent; ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum; carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models; converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient. Measurements it carries. Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type, against which the depth profile is checked; Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille; the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures; Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters; five published spectra of the absorption of pure water, Pope & Fry (1997), Smith & Baker (1981), Mason, Cone & Fry (2016), Lee et al. (2015) and Morel et al. (2007), for the caller to choose from; the eight stations of the clearest ocean water measured, Morel et al. (2007); the measured reflectance of ten materials found in and around water, from the USGS Spectral Library Version 7, for reference images of how they look through each water type. Without a water type. It gives: Kd from the chlorophyll concentration of case 1 water (Morel & Maritorena 2001, and the earlier edition of Morel 1988), or from the absorption and backscattering coefficients and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2013); the attenuation of the visible and of the whole shortwave from the surface to a depth, and the depth where a given fraction of the visible light is left, the euphotic depth among them, from the absorption and backscattering coefficients at 490 nm and the sun (Lee et al. 2005, 2007); from chlorophyll, the absorption by phytoplankton (Bricaud et al. 1995) and the b
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: Vision-model-based robotic navigation has gained increasing popularity, yet existing approaches still struggle to deliver effective and efficient navigation performance, \textit{e.g.}, diffusion-based policies that require costly iterative denoising. In this work, we propose three improvements to bridge these gaps. First, we adopt a rectified flow framework to reduce the required inference steps to one while achieving comparable or even superior performance. Second, we leverage a bidirectional Mamba-based visual encoder that employs selective state-space modeling to more effectively capture bidirectional temporal dependencies across observation frames, even with longer input sequences. Most importantly, we find that naïvely combining these two components to balance accuracy with inference speed yields no further performance gains or even produces inferior results. Upon extensive analysis, we realized that the root cause lies in the fact that the Hydra-derived temporal context is shared unchanged across all flow timesteps, and timestep information is introduced only within the velocity network. This weak coupling limits the model's ability to adaptively exploit temporal visual features at different flow states. To address this, we propose a feature-wise timestep conditioning design that explicitly conditions the visual embedding on the flow timestep, enabling noise-level-aware trajectory generation, thereby restoring a meaningful gradient pathway and enabling coherent interaction between the rectified flow and the temporal encoder. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms both baseline and competitive methods.
title: Inject, Encode, Navigate: Feature-Wise Time Injection for Rectified Flow with Bidirectional Feature Encoding

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent each image with hundreds of visual tokens, which can make inference costly even when a prompt depends on only part of the image. Dynamic Token Merging (DTM), introduced in MrT5 for byte-level text encoders, learns which tokens to remove: a lightweight delete gate scores contextualized hidden states, acts as a differentiable attention bias during training, and physically removes tokens at inference. We argue that DTM is a general token deletion framework rather than a byte-level technique, and extend it to the vision modality and to decoder-only models. Applying DTM to T5Gemma 2 and Gemma 3 yields V-MrT5Gemma2, which deletes visual tokens inside a bidirectional multimodal encoder, and V-MrGemma3, which compacts the prompt and its key-value caches during decoder-only prefill. Across ten benchmarks, DTM's advantage over attention-based and random deletion grows with the deletion rate and is largest on document, chart, and scene-text reading. At 80% visual token deletion (approximately 60% fewer FLOPs), DTM raises accuracy over FastV from 51.8 to 63.0 on ChartQA and from 63.3 to 67.8 on TextVQA with V-MrT5Gemma2, as well as from 62.2 to 68.8 and from 71.2 to 75.1 with V-MrGemma3, retaining 90-96% of unpruned performance on both tasks with significant efficiency gains. These results support DTM as a general framework for efficient transformers.
title: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Vision-Language Models

summary: Strain localization is often associated with plastic flow and permanent deformation. Here we show that a tensile neck in a crosslinked nematic network can undergo nearly complete recovery through reverse phase-boundary motion, leaving little residual deformation. In a monodomain liquid crystal elastomer stretched perpendicular to its initial director, this recovery occurs during an isothermal loading-unloading cycle. Digital image correlation resolves the process as the retreat of interfaces separating low- and high-stretch regions, where the high-stretch domain shrinks while previously necked material thickens, despite substantial mechanical hysteresis. Within the recoverable-necking regime, increasing temperature lowers the loading plateau stress but raises the unloading plateau stress. A nonconvex constitutive description provides an energetic basis for the coexistence of the two stretch states, while gradient regularization accounts for the finite width of their interfaces through an equilibrium reference profile. These results identify the spatial mechanism of neck recovery and distinguish recoverable strain localization from mechanical reversibility in an orientationally ordered polymer network.
title: Recoverable Necking Enabled by Reverse Phase-Boundary Motion in Liquid Crystal Elastomers

summary: Grain boundaries (GBs) govern many properties of polycrystalline materials, and inverse design would make the GB structure itself a design variable. Crystal generative models such as MatterGen operate on periodic cells, which contain two GBs. The cell energy defines a single GB only when the two are equivalent, but existing models do not enforce this equivalence. Building on MatterGen, we developed a symmetry-constrained diffusion model in which the two GBs are related by a symmetry operation: atoms near one GB are generated, and those near the other are reconstructed through a symmetry projection applied at every denoising step. We applied it to the $Σ5(210)[001]$ symmetric tilt GB in Al, conditioning generation on the GB energy from a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). All 350 generated structures kept a geometrically equivalent GB pair after relaxation. Given a target GB energy, the model generated structures at that energy: for the three in-range targets with many nearby training structures, 44% to 70% fell within $\pm 0.1$ J/m$^2$ of the target. Tracking weakened at higher energies and failed outside the training range. Of the 91 near-target structures, 90 matched no training structure under the adopted geometric criterion, indicating that the model can propose configurations near the target energy that are distinct from the training structures, a capability that could help identify unknown metastable GB structures observed in experiments. Building GB-pair equivalence into generation thus makes GB properties well-defined design targets, enabling inverse design of GB structures.
title: Generating grain boundary structures at a specified energy with a symmetry-constrained diffusion model

summary: We investigate the information retained by fuzzy-point specialization in Chang fuzzy topologies and the fibers realizing a prescribed Gödel specialization relation. Every reflexive, minimum-transitive fuzzy preorder has a greatest stratified Chang realization. Its realization fiber is a singleton precisely for the constant relation $1$; otherwise, below each member lies a continuum-sized descending chain with no lower bound in the fiber, also within the Alexandrov subclass. On finite support sets, every nontrivial stratified fiber has cardinality continuum without assuming Alexandrov completeness; this remains true for Alexandrov fibers on countable sets. We describe the entire two-point Alexandrov fiber order as the reverse of a product of classes of join-preserving threshold functions. For arbitrary Chang topologies, quasi-specialization determines membership specialization and its kernel completion, which in turn determine Gödel specialization; the converse determinations fail in general. A central reconstruction result identifies the greatest quasi-specialization realization by \emph{exact agreement on every one- or two-point restriction}, equivalently by closure in a product of discrete grade intervals. In particular, quasi-specialization determines every Chang topology on a finite support set. We also represent general Alexandrov Chang topologies by matrices of join-preserving threshold maps and isolate the additional scalar compatibility law required for reconstruction from the graded relation. These results separate information encoded by finite-coordinate point comparisons from global restrictions on fuzzy open families.
title: Threshold Representations and Realization Fibers of Specialization in Chang Fuzzy Topologies

summary: Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal. As a remedy, we study a convex combination between the individual risk, i.e. the average log loss of the individual particles, and the mixture risk. At the particle level, this regularised risk imposes a reverse-KL barrier on the responsibilities of the particles, so that no particle can be starved of training signal. These phenomena are illustrated in two case studies: In the first, a predictively-oriented posterior is computed using mean-field Langevin dynamics, and the numerics are well-behaved only when our regularisation is employed. In the second, ensembles of low-rank adapters are jointly fine-tuned on large language models, across four backbones and eight multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks; direct minimisation of the mixture risk leads to responsibility starvation, whose severity decreases as the competence of the backbone increases, whereas our regularised estimator attains a lower held-out mixture risk on every backbone considered.
title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures

summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.
title: Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials

summary: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. Candidate graph elements are validated against predefined schemas and consolidated through scope-aware exact, normalized, fuzzy, embedding-based, and LLM-assisted entity resolution. Temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, conflict-aware property management, and fine-grained provenance preserve issuer identity, reporting-period validity, and traceability to source evidence. The contributions of this work comprise the proposed methodology for financial knowledge graph construction, the creation of an evidence-grounded temporal knowledge graph from heterogeneous financial documents, and an intrinsic framework for evaluating the quality of the resulting graph. The evaluation framework assesses seven weighted dimensions, two hard validation gates, and structural diagnostics. By separating graph-quality assessment from downstream retrieval and answer generation, the framework supports systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of the constructed graph.
title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation

summary: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. Documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) are reconstructed into hierarchical section trees and indexed with structured metadata. Retrieval is supported by two domain-specific embedding models fine-tuned on domain data (water and climate). On top of this knowledge base, a ReAct-style controller iteratively orchestrates retrieval actions by allocating retrieval budget across domain collections and accumulating evidence until a stopping criterion is met. In a retrieval benchmark over the corpus, the proposed approach improves Mean Reciprocal Rank by 26.7% (relative) compared to a single-domain embedding baseline, indicating more consistent retrieval of relevant evidence to support cross-project knowledge synthesis and climate-resilient decision-making.
title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem

summary: Powerful generative models including large language and vision models have demonstrated success across a wide range of content generation, editing and manipulation tasks via end-to-end prompt-based generation. However, current assessment of the quality of generative content manipulation remains subjective, limiting scientific understanding of model capabilities. Inspired by rate-distortion theory from Shannon information compression theory, in this work we formalize hierarchical content summarization as an information encoding problem. We design a principled framework to extract the semantic hierarchy of the source content to support quantitative characterization of the rate-distortion trade-off between compression efficiency (rate) against information loss (distortion) during generative content manipulation, which allows us to benchmark various models with respect to performance conditional on rate budget of interest. We demonstrate the use of the framework with empirical experiments on content summarization for long-context question-answering with state-of-the-art large language models, offering new insights into their efficiency and comprehension capabilities. We further demonstrate the use of the semantic hierarchy as guidance for performing effective retrieval augmented generation, showing improved rate-distortion characteristics against current baselines.
title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization

summary: Analysis code for the manuscript "A trogocytosis-related four-gene signature stratifies prognosis and delineates immune evasion and a resistance-leaning drug-response profile in gastric cancer" (Frontiers in Immunology, manuscript ID 2035159).
